chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had a Wars-dyed sheet that he would wear among his family until it turned against his body.
And he (the narrator) said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'We used to wear dyed clothing at home.'

key_terms.الْمُعَصْفَرَ: Garments dyed with 'usfur (safflower) or with any bright coloring; commonly used to indicate dyed or saffron-colored clothing
key_terms.مِلْحَفَةٌ مُوَرَّسَةٌ: A sheet or outer garment dyed with wars, a plant used in Yemen to produce a yellow-orange hue
key_terms.يَرْدَعَ: To turn or wrap around; here describing the sheet being worn until it rested on the body

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet wear dyed clothing at home?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) wore a sheet dyed with wars (a yellow-orange plant dye from Yemen) in the privacy of his home. Imam al-Baqir (AS) then adds that the Imams themselves wore dyed garments at home. This hadith establishes the permissibility of wearing colorful or dyed clothing in the domestic setting, even if scholars debate its suitability for public worship contexts.
